script.title: Why space is freezing if the Sun is so hot
sentences: The Sun's surface is about 5,500 degrees Celsius, yet space is brutally cold.
The secret is that heat needs something to travel through.
On Earth, air and water carry heat from atom to atom.
Space is almost a perfect vacuum, with nearly nothing to carry it.
So sunlight only heats what it hits directly.
That's why the sunny side of the space station can pass 120 degrees, while the shade drops far below freezing.
Astronauts survive with suits that reflect light and carefully move heat around.
Hot and freezing at the same time. Which side would you pick?

script.title: What if Earth stopped spinning?
sentences: If Earth suddenly stopped spinning, would you stop with it?
This thought experiment needs a rule: imagine the solid ground stops, but the air and oceans initially keep moving.
Their existing motion would drive catastrophic winds and water movement relative to the suddenly stationary surface.
The effect would depend on latitude, because the surface’s rotational speed is greatest near the equator.
Stopping gradually would be a different scenario, with very different consequences for people and infrastructure.
Longer-term sunlight patterns would also change, though Earth would still travel around the Sun.
There is no realistic ordinary event that simply switches off Earth’s rotation, so this is hypothetical physics.
Would you choose to explain the wind or the changing daylight next?
